blocks.text: URIJAH SON OF SHEMAIAH OF KIRJATH-JEARIM · TWO KINGDOMS
Urijah. He prophesied as Jeremiah did, fled to Egypt, and was brought back and killed by Jehoiakim.
SCRIPTURE CALLS
Prophet
ERA
Two kingdoms 930–586 BC
IN THE DAYS OF
Jehoiakim
BOOK
None bears the name
HOW THE WORD CAME
“There was also a man that prophesied in the name of the LORD, Urijah”.
THE CALL
How the word came
“There was also a man that prophesied in the name of the LORD, Urijah”. Jeremiah 26:20
BEFORE THE KINGS
Before Jehoiakim
KING OF JUDAH
Jehoiakim
“who slew him with the sword, and cast his dead body into the graves of the common people.”
Jeremiah 26:23 (KJV) →
THE MESSAGE
The word in its main themes
Against the city and the land
PLACES
Where his story happened
Kirjath-jearim · His home
Egypt · Where he fled and was taken
Jerusalem · Where Jehoiakim reigned; Jeremiah 26:23 says only that Urijah was brought “unto Jehoiakim the king” and killed
COMPANIONS AND OPPONENTS
Who stood with him, and against him
Jeremiah
Elnathan son of Achbor
Shemaiah, his father
HOW THE STORY ENDS
Scripture says, tradition says
SCRIPTURE SAYS
Brought back from Egypt to Jehoiakim, “who slew him with the sword, and cast his dead body into the graves of the common people”. Jeremiah 26:23
TRADITION SAYS
No tradition is recorded here.
OPEN QUESTIONS
Where readers have differed
The writer, to show Jeremiah's danger
Ellicott's commentary; C. F. Keil (1874–1880); the Pulpit Commentary; A. W. Streane (1913)

It is not part of the elders' speech: Ellicott says it “cannot be regarded as part of the argument of the ‘elders’”; Streane: “The story is introduced by the compiler (probably Baruch) to illustrate the risk to which Jeremiah was exposed”; Keil: to show “the hostility of King Jehoiakim”. Jeremiah 26:20–24 [20][63][99][102]
The elders, as a warning
R. Jamieson, A. R. Fausset and D. Brown (1871); one opinion reported by Joseph Benson
JFB: the context “implies rather that the words are the continuation of the previous speech of the elders”: Urijah suffered, and they imply that “sin has been added”. Jeremiah 26:17–23 [54][6]
Jeremiah's accusers, as a precedent for death
Matthew Poole (1683–1685); John Gill (1748–1763), after Kimchi and Rashi
Poole: “the words of some others … urging a later precedent, in the time of Jehoiakim”; Gill reports Kimchi and Jarchi (Rashi) reading it so. Jeremiah 26:20–23 [85][39]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 1
Jeremiah 26
PASSAGES · 1
Jeremiah 26:20–24
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Jeremiah does not record any of Urijah's words, only that they agreed with Jeremiah's.
It does not give the year of his death; the chapter's opening date (“the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim”, Jeremiah 26:1) belongs to Jeremiah's own trial.
Scripture does not say he was beheaded; it says Jehoiakim “slew him with the sword”.
